question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 25 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely increased the load on the system.
why_chain: The marketing campaign went live at the right time and place (162 minutes before the change).
The increase in request volume and error rate are consistent with a sudden surge in traffic.
The rise in p95 latency is also consistent with increased load on the system.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The change point is at the right time and place, and the increase in latency is a symptom, not a cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The config change caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The change point is at the right time and place, and the increase in latency is a symptom, not a cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The dependency issue caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The increase in latency is a symptom, not a cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The data quality issue caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The increase in latency is a symptom, not a cause.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 219 ms (+60%), with a change point at 2026-03-25T08:10:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2048 per 5 min before, 9799 per 5 min after, +379%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.37% before, 0.74% after, +102%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 08:10 UTC (eu-west; 162 min before the change; record R011; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R012; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (162 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Review and optimize the autoscaler configuration to ensure it scales in a timely manner.
Monitor the marketing campaigns and adjust the autoscaler accordingly to avoid similar issues in the future.
Review and possibly reduce the flash sale campaign duration to avoid similar spikes in traffic.
